lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Let's call this meeting to order. Welcome here, everyone. Council, tonight's my turn to do opening, and I've— as I've read the agenda, went through the entire book and pamphlet, I realized that today I have opening, so I'm going to tell you a story. About a month ago, I turned 60. This was the birthday that was hard for me. 40 was easy, 50 was easy, but 60 was difficult. And I've been thinking a lot about this, and 26 years ago, my dad passed away at 65. So I always thought, you know, they always tell you that if you want to know how old you're going to get, you just look at how old your dad got. That's right. And so I thought, man, if I got 5 years left, that's going to be tough. And I think that's why it's been difficult for me. But through that all, I've been thinking a lot about my dad. And he spent— he died of pancreatic cancer. He spent 8 months in palliative care in our hospital. And every night, we would go visit him. And every night, as we were saying goodnight, When I was getting— my mom was getting ready and I was taking her home, my dad would always call me over and in a quiet voice he would give me little tidbits of wisdom. And some of those tidbits of wisdom, one of them that really stands out to me was he told me, he said, Earl, there's 2 kinds of people in this world. And he said, imagine you're on a ladder. Okay, imagine that you're climbing up the ladder and there's someone on the roof and they're reaching over with their hand to help you. He said, that's one kind of the people— that's one kind of person that's in this world. And then he said, there's also another kind of person. He said, imagine you're on that same ladder and you're climbing up, but there's someone reaching up and grabbing your heels. Oh. And trying to pull you down. So that's another kind of person in this world. Then he said, what I want you to do, Earl, I want you to go home and I want you to decide what kind of person you want to be. Don't, don't wait until the opportunity arises. I want you to decide in the quietness of when you're alone, who you wanna be, what kind of person you wanna be. And he did that to me every night that— of those 8 months. He left me with a little tidbit of wisdom. And many of those tidbits had choices, came with choices. And so— Go home. I did go home and I did think about that. And in the quietness, I made that decision to be the person I wanted to be. You know, and sometimes I actually am that person. Like, it's still difficult, even when you make— even when you decide to be a certain way, it's still— when you're faced with that decision, it can still be difficult to follow that decision through. Thank you. But my, my, uh, when I think of, of that and I think of my dad and I know that all he was trying to do in those 8 months was he's trying to leave me with the tools to be the man that he, that he was hoping I would ever turn out to be. And it's kind of sad because in In 20— in 2000, he passed away. In 2005, we started the store. In 2010, I got elected to council. In 2018, I got elected as mayor, you know, and, and he's missed all those good things. So there is one day I'm literally looking forward to going to heaven, running to his room wherever he is, and, and telling him all the things that He missed and the things we've done, and hopefully we can celebrate together. Thank you very much. Council, we've got the agenda in front of us, looking for a motion to adopt. Councillor Penner. Second by Councillor Penner. Call for the question. All those in favor? Opposed? That was carried. We've got the minutes of July 21st, 2026, regular council meeting. Looking for a motion to approve. Second. Second by Councillor Hiebert. Call for the question. All those in favor? Opposed? That is carried. We've got the— is there any business arising from the minutes? Okay, seeing none, we will continue. We'll go directly— we are at 7:35, so we'll go directly into the public hearing. This is 6A. This is rezoning bylaw 2283. This is referring to Williams Creek Phase 1. At this time, I will close the council meeting and open the public hearing. Mr. Warkentin, could you please introduce this file?

lines.text: Council, I've— again, I just want to thank everyone for coming out and speaking their piece. And call for the question. All those in favour? Opposed? That is carried. Move on to 7A. lines.text: Thank you so much.

lines.speaker: Justus Oladele
lines.title: Founder
lines.label: Justus Oladele (Founder, KodaGo)
lines.text: Thank you for the opportunity to stand before this great council. Okay, my name is Justice Oladele and I'm the founder of Coda Go. Behind me is my partner [name withheld] and my wife and baby [name withheld] and [name withheld]. So it's such a great honor and privilege to be in your midst today. Okay, I just quickly want to just run through what CoderGo is, and I want to believe some of us here may have been getting some pings on their phone about CoderGo in Steinbach, right? Yes. So, um, 2 years ago I came into this beautiful city from Montreal. So I lived in Montreal for some months, originally from Nigeria, and, um, a friend of mine invited me to come to Steinbach. Like, I didn't know where Steinbach was on the map, right? So when, when I didn't ask, I didn't ask, where do you live in, in, I mean, in Manitoba? Yeah. come to Manitoba. And just like every other person, if you live outside of Manitoba, people think that everybody who lives in Manitoba lives in Winnipeg. So I never, I never asked— anyway, she's just sitting here. So I never asked, where do you live? So when I landed in Winnipeg with my wife, we started asking very weird questions like, can I get a train ticket to Steinbach? People said no, no train, no trains, no underground train to Steinbach. Can I get a flight ticket to Steinbach? And no, no flight ticket to Steinbach. Okay, can I get a bus to Steinbach?

lines.speaker: Justus Oladele
lines.title: Founder
lines.label: Justus Oladele (Founder, KodaGo)
lines.text: No bus to Steinbach.

lines.speaker: Justus Oladele
lines.title: Founder
lines.label: Justus Oladele (Founder, KodaGo)
lines.text: Okay, can I get—

lines.speaker: Justus Oladele
lines.title: Founder
lines.label: Justus Oladele (Founder, KodaGo)
lines.text: What about Uber?

lines.speaker: Justus Oladele
lines.title: Founder
lines.label: Justus Oladele (Founder, KodaGo)
lines.text: Um, yeah, well, you can get to Steinbach, but you can't get back. So yeah, but finally she sent her husband to come pick us at the airport. Wow. And yeah, we landed in Steinbach. Beautiful city. It has literally everything you need except public transportation, which is not bad. Every city is designed uniquely, right? And our first very ugly experience happened when we used one of the common transportation services in the city. And it was around a very cold period. And we— I think she was still pregnant at that time. So we stayed outside in the cold waiting for so long, and this guy showed up with a few other passengers and all that. And so from there, we started hearing different complaints of other persons and all that, complaints about, you know, lack of comfort and all that. So the frustration was really building in, in my mind of, now imagine coming from a, from a very big city that has underground train and everything, and here you started your life all over again. So I wanted to leave.

lines.speaker: Justus Oladele
lines.title: Founder
lines.label: Justus Oladele (Founder, KodaGo)
lines.text: Then one day a thought just flashed in my mind. Okay, now back to my background.

lines.speaker: Justus Oladele
lines.title: Founder
lines.label: Justus Oladele (Founder, KodaGo)
lines.text: I studied computer science and I have been a software developer for quite a number of years. And so the thought was like, Instead of running away from the problem, why don't you just solve it? Then I remember coming to meet the mayor of Steinbach, and is there a reason why we don't have Uber in Steinbach?

lines.speaker: Justus Oladele
lines.title: Founder
lines.label: Justus Oladele (Founder, KodaGo)
lines.text: And I started making some personal research.

lines.speaker: Justus Oladele
lines.title: Founder
lines.label: Justus Oladele (Founder, KodaGo)
lines.text: I discovered that Uber does not go to any city that is less than 50,000 people. So that was a big problem.

lines.speaker: Justus Oladele
lines.title: Founder
lines.label: Justus Oladele (Founder, KodaGo)
lines.text: Now, and— Can we do this?

lines.speaker: Justus Oladele
lines.title: Founder
lines.label: Justus Oladele (Founder, KodaGo)
lines.text: He said, oh yeah, they are open for innovation and all that. So we, for a short time, I sat with my team and we built CoderGo. CoderGo is not a foreign app that came to Steinbach or Canada. This is a Steinbach-built app for local, serving the local community and connecting other communities to the cities and all that. Wow. So when we built that and we started testing, we started taking opinions of people and getting reviews and all that. And today I'm glad to share that this minute we have about 246 users who have signed up on CodaGo. Now, connecting the entire Southeast Manitoba, connecting the Other cities to major cities like Winnipeg and all that. Few— I think last week we have riders who rode from Steinbach to the airport. Now, the idea is not just to create a product, but we wanted to create a product that is local, that is serving our own people. Now, just a point of notice, the 2 biggest rideshare companies in Canada, which is both— I mean— Uber. Lyft and Uber. These are American products. We're talking about where is the Canadian product. We don't have any except CodaGo. So this is not just an app that is built just like every other app, but this is a local app built right here in Steinbach.

lines.speaker: Justus Oladele
lines.title: Founder
lines.label: Justus Oladele (Founder, KodaGo)
lines.text: So, and I know some of us have questions and want to know much about the product and how it's designed to help the community.

lines.speaker: Justus Oladele
lines.title: Founder
lines.label: Justus Oladele (Founder, KodaGo)
lines.text: So I'll be willing to take your questions.

lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Okay, council, any questions for Justice?

lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Damian Penner (Councillor)
lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. Not so much a question but more, more a comment. Justice, I appreciate you coming out and making a presentation to us. Yes, I have seen your advertisements online and the correspondence, and it's definitely piqued my interest. And as a small business owner myself, this is a prime example of Private innovation— Yes. Is often far superior to public spent dollars. Correct. That's not to say that public transit isn't something in the future that the city won't look at, but private innovation finds gaps in the market and brings a phenomenal product, innovation in technology, and I really, really wish you all the best going forward, and I hope this is incredibly successful, and I appreciate that it's a homegrown Yeah. In Steinbach. That's not something that you hear a lot of in our community, is homegrown Steinbach technology businesses. So I just want to give, give, give you, give you credit where credit is due, and, and wish you all the best. Thank you.

lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Go ahead.

lines.text: Hello, Justice.

lines.speaker: Justus Oladele
lines.title: Founder
lines.label: Justus Oladele (Founder, KodaGo)
lines.text: Thank you, sir.

lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Jake Hiebert (Councillor) [medium]
lines.text: You and I have met before. I sat through one of your presentations at the event center. Yeah, a 3-hour one. And so I think all my questions were answered there, so I have no questions for you today.

lines.speaker: Justus Oladele
lines.title: Founder
lines.label: Justus Oladele (Founder, KodaGo) [medium]
lines.text: Oh, thank you, sir.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor

lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Bill Hiebert (Councillor) [medium]
lines.text: Through you, Mr. Mayor, Justice, welcome here. My question is, I mean, my comment first is a lot of people ask about Uber. No, we don't have Uber. Yeah, so how does it compare to a taxi ride price-wise?

lines.speaker: Justus Oladele
lines.title: Founder
lines.label: Justus Oladele (Founder, KodaGo)
lines.text: Okay, price-wise.

lines.speaker: Justus Oladele
lines.title: Founder
lines.label: Justus Oladele (Founder, KodaGo)
lines.text: Yeah, so, and okay, one of, first, one of the difference of CodaGo different from taxi is that unlike conventional taxi companies, yeah, sometimes it's based on meters and based on time, and then you have to get to the destination to know what you— to pay. But with CodaGo, you can know your price upfront from the app. That is one.

lines.speaker: Justus Oladele
lines.title: Founder
lines.label: Justus Oladele (Founder, KodaGo)
lines.text: And we, as a local product designed for local community, we try to ensure that we make it a very—

lines.speaker: Justus Oladele
lines.title: Founder
lines.label: Justus Oladele (Founder, KodaGo)
lines.text: Like, regulate what— sometimes we don't want people to take advantage of the people. At the same time, we also want to ensure that the drivers who are the cost-bearing also have value for their service. So in turn with that, we're also creating jobs for private people as well. So this is one of the—

lines.speaker: Justus Oladele
lines.title: Founder
lines.label: Justus Oladele (Founder, KodaGo)
lines.text: And also, there's something we launched recently which is called the student rides.

lines.speaker: Justus Oladele
lines.title: Founder
lines.label: Justus Oladele (Founder, KodaGo)
lines.text: So, and, um, we really want to appreciate the fact that a city like Steinbach is giving a very fair playing ground for local businesses like this, unlike some cities have different regulations, different city regulations, and that is really weighing down local businesses.

lines.speaker: Justus Oladele
lines.title: Founder
lines.label: Justus Oladele (Founder, KodaGo)
lines.text: So, um, so KodaGo is looking forward to partnering with the city to ensure that we're able to serve the underserved And ensuring that everybody, you know, whether you're a rider or you're a driver, you're getting values as well. Wow. Yeah. Thank you.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Anything further? Go ahead.

lines.speaker: Susan Penner
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Susan Penner (Councillor)
lines.text: Congratulations. This is amazing. That's quite an accomplishment.

lines.speaker: Susan Penner
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Susan Penner (Councillor)
lines.text: Thank you. So first of all, congratulations with that.

lines.speaker: Susan Penner
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Susan Penner (Councillor)
lines.text: Do you have plans to expand and make this national? There's a lot of cities of 50,000 or less. Is that kind of your target to stick with this? smaller cities?

lines.speaker: Susan Penner
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Susan Penner (Councillor)
lines.text: Are you planning to expand?

lines.speaker: Susan Penner
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Susan Penner (Councillor) [medium]
lines.text: What do you—

lines.title: Founder
lines.label: Justus Oladele (Founder, KodaGo)
lines.text: Okay, thank you for— are you done? Thank you so much for that. I think we got the approval, right? We've just gotten the approval to serve the city of Winkler. And in the shortest time, we're also getting requirements from the city of Winnipeg as well. So, and so this just an idea that started from, I mean, Steinbach and now serving other cities as well. So yeah, the, the dream has always been to connect, um, the entire underserved cities across Manitoba. Yeah.

lines.speaker: Susan Penner
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Susan Penner (Councillor)
lines.text: That's wonderful. All the best.

lines.speaker: Justus Oladele
lines.title: Founder
lines.label: Justus Oladele (Founder, KodaGo)
lines.text: Thank you.

lines.title: Mayor

lines.title: Founder
lines.label: Justus Oladele (Founder, KodaGo)

lines.speaker: Justus Oladele
lines.title: Founder
lines.label: Justus Oladele (Founder, KodaGo)
lines.text: Which is a city partnership, and a city partnership that can accelerate local growth.

lines.speaker: Justus Oladele
lines.title: Founder
lines.label: Justus Oladele (Founder, KodaGo) [medium]
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: Justus Oladele
lines.title: Founder
lines.label: Justus Oladele (Founder, KodaGo)
lines.text: One of which is, one of them is like city recognition, right?

lines.speaker: Justus Oladele
lines.title: Founder
lines.label: Justus Oladele (Founder, KodaGo)
lines.text: It is, I'm so amazed that a lot of people get, we get calls and emails from outside of Steinbach and many people still don't know that this is a Steinbach-built product, right?

lines.speaker: Justus Oladele
lines.title: Founder
lines.label: Justus Oladele (Founder, KodaGo)
lines.text: Whenever we hear big giant apps like Uber, we think of California. They have an identity, right? So we are seeking a collaboration. lines.title: Mayor

lines.text: Okay, that, that, um, we— you know what, what I'll need to do is, uh, meet with you and, and maybe you can write a letter Explaining what that's supposed to look like. Okay. And it's, that would go beyond a letter of support, right? Yeah. And so we don't, right now, we don't have that partnership with any local transportation agency. businesses other than our, I guess, our Handy Transit, accessible transit, which is subsidized by the province, right, for exactly those that are the people that are mobility challenged, right? But I do want to say, Justice, thank you, and I'm— for meeting with you like 2 years ago and seeing this slowly develop over time. Yes. You've taken advice and direction from many different people and you've had other partners that didn't work out and now I see you with [name withheld] and we know [name withheld] quite well. Yeah. And it's, no, it's great to see this homegrown tech business that you've done. You saw, like, as Councillor Penner stated, you saw a need and that's, That's what private enterprise does. Going into Winkler is a very— it's a similar city like us. Yeah. And I can see that they would have need for it as well. Yeah. And so, yeah, wishing you all the best. Thank you.

lines.title: Founder
lines.label: Justus Oladele (Founder, KodaGo)
lines.text: Thank you so much, sir.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor

lines.text: And, uh, yeah, I'm— I've been, uh, I'm very glad that we've been able to become friends and that you've been, uh, we've been able to have the relationship we do have. Thank you.

lines.title: Founder

lines.speaker: Jake Hiebert

lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. We've obviously discussed this, the bylaw earlier, both at our SPC meeting and when we gave first reading. lines.speaker: Michael Zwaagstra
lines.title: Councillor

lines.text: Anything further, council? Anything? Nope. Call for the question. All those in favor? Opposed? That is carried. And we'll go directly into third reading. Looking for a motion to approve. Second by Councillor Hiebert. Go ahead.

lines.speaker: Damian Penner
lines.title: Councillor

lines.text: I have nothing further to add.

lines.speaker: Bill Hiebert

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Okay, call for the question. All those in favor of third reading? Opposed? That is carried. We've got 9E. This is bylaw 2282. This is administrative penalty bylaw schedule, and this we're also going to do second and third reading. Mr. Warkentin, could you please introduce this one?

lines.speaker: Troy Warkentin
lines.title: City Manager
lines.label: Troy Warkentin (City Manager)
lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. In order for the city to actually proceed with enforcement actions, and particularly with respect to fines, that are listed in the bylaw that council just approved. It also requires the update— sorry, amendment and update to the city's administrative penalty bylaw. That is presented on page 116. The changes that are being proposed are highlighted in yellow on page 121. Recommendation is that council give this bylaw second and third readings.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Warkentin. Council, how would you like to proceed?

lines.speaker: Damian Penner
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Damian Penner (Councillor)
lines.text: Motion to approve.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Second by Councillor Hiebert. Go ahead.

lines.speaker: Damian Penner
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Damian Penner (Councillor)
lines.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Mayor. This update to the penalty bylaw schedule is to reflect the land drainage bylaw that was just passed. In order for there to be some teeth to the bylaw, there needs to be a potential for penalties that go with it. Aside from Parking infractions, the history of the city has been, and I hope will continue to be, to first educate and then enforce and then penalize. And I expect that will be going forward with this as well. This isn't to have our inspectors going out looking for individuals to penalize, but rather to have the opportunity to encourage them stronger to get their work done.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor

lines.speaker: Troy Warkentin
lines.title: City Manager
lines.label: Troy Warkentin (City Manager)
lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. The owner of this particular property is 3XL Holdings Ltd., and the applicant for the rezoning is [name withheld]. Bylaw 2285 seeks to rezone the subject property from RLD residential low density to RMD, residential medium density, to allow multifamily development. Recommendation is for council to give this bylaw first reading so that a public hearing may be scheduled for later on this fall.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Warkentin. Council, how would you like to proceed? Councillor Siemens?

lines.speaker: Jac Siemens
lines.title: Councillor

lines.text: Motion to approve first reading.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Seconded by Councillor Penner.

lines.speaker: Jac Siemens
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Jac Siemens (Councillor)
lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. This is a large lot on Giesbrecht that has a single-family home on it, but it is a Very large lot, and they're looking to build a 12-unit structure. So we— in order— we need to pass this in order to get it to a public hearing, and the proposal will be subject to the city's infill policies. So I would also like to hear what the public has to say.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Anything further? Nothing further. Any further, council? Anything in closing?

lines.speaker: Jac Siemens

lines.text: No, sir.
